unit_title: Safe Start: Personal Movement Readiness and Self-Management
standards: Michigan PE Standard 3: Demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical fitness. [Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 1 (foundational high-school physical education)]
Michigan PE Standard 4: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others. [Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 1 (foundational high-school physical education)]

Michigan PE Standard 5: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction. [Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 1 (foundational high-school physical education)]

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of self-directed warm-up and cool-down design in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe effort scales described by feel, breath, and speech rather than by device using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply the stop rule: pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, unsafe conditions in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving space, surface, footwear, weather, and equipment checks; correct it and explain why.
Connect hydration and recovery around activity with setting a personal starting point without comparison and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Design and run a personal warm-up, effort-management, and stop-rule routine, then revise it after using it across several sessions. Evidence is the written or described routine and its revision, not a measured result.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with safe, independent application and adequate explanation of cues, tactics, or training reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign varied practice and a fresh transfer check on a later occasion.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the simplest version and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source on one occasion, not the sole basis for long-term mastery. Never adjust a score for body size, weight, or appearance.

accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
inclusion_note: The learner sets their own starting point; no baseline is compared to any other learner, to a norm table, or to a prior year.
